description.value: The study investigated subjective craving and brain responses to heroin-related cues in former heroin addicts receiving long-term methadone maintenance treatment.

spans.text: To investigate the subjective craving and brain response to heroin-related cues in former heroin addicts on long-term methadone maintenance treatment.

value: We hypothesized that brain regions previously found to be involved in the processing of addictive cues would maintain their activated responses to visual heroin-related stimuli in formerly heroin-dependent patients on long-term MMT.
Furthermore, we hypothesized that this activation would be present during methadone daily dosing (when methadone is presumably at a stable level).

definition.value: Brain responses to heroin-related stimuli were significantly higher than neutral stimuli.

spans.text: Brain responses to heroin-related stimuli were significantly higher than neutral stimuli ( p < .0001, uncorrected) in the bilateral ACC, DLPFC, fusiform, postcentral gyrus, posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), precuneus, thalamus, inferior temporal gyrus, middle occipital gyrus, middle temporal gyrus, inferior occipital gyrus, superior parietal lobule, left caudate, putamen, inferior parietal gyrus, and pons ( and ).

value: The results indicate that the learned brain response of former heroin addicts to drug-related stimuli may persist despite long-term methadone maintenance treatment.

spans.text: Conclusions and Scientific Significance: The results indicate that the learned brain response of former heroin addicts to drug-related stimuli may persist despite long-term methadone maintenance treatment.
